column1: How do I apply for a service dog?
column2: Fill out ISD's online application. You'll find the link on the Apply for a Service Dog page. If you have questions about your application, email applicants@illiniservicedogs.com.

column1: How much does a service dog cost me?
column2: Nothing. Illini Service Dogs places its dogs 100% free of charge. The program is paid for entirely by donations.

column1: Who can get a service dog from ISD?
column2: ISD trains mobility service dogs for people with physical disabilities who could benefit from one. The Apply for a Service Dog page explains the process. If you're not sure whether ISD is a fit for you, email applicants@illiniservicedogs.com.

column1: How long is the wait for a service dog?
column2: ISD does not quote wait times and does not go first come, first served. Matches are made each year based on applicants' needs and which dogs are nearing the end of their training. We encourage applicants to also pursue other service dog programs at the same time.

column1: How are dogs matched with applicants?
column2: Once a year, ISD matches applicants with dogs that are nearing the end of training. Matches are based on each applicant's needs and each dog's skills, not on when you applied.

column1: What is a puppy raiser?
column2: Puppy raisers care for an ISD dog in training in their own home. ISD dogs are in the program from about 8 weeks to 2.5 years old, and a puppy raising placement usually lasts 2 to 6 months.

column1: What is Illini Service Dogs?
column2: Illini Service Dogs is a nonprofit and student organization at the University of Illinois. It was founded in 2010 by Bridget Evans, inspired by her service dog Coal. ISD trains mobility service dogs and places them free of charge with people who have physical disabilities.
